newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile approves Codelco 1997 investment plan.
newsitem.headline: Chile approves Codelco 1997 investment plan.

text.p: The Chilean government has approved an investment plan of $720 million for state copper giant Codelco this year, although the figure was $100 million less than Codelco had sought, said a top official.

The lower figure this year will not have any impact on the corporation's overall investment program which will boost copper production to 1.4 million tonnes by 2000, said budget director Mario Marcel.
The decision to give the go-ahead to a lower budget is part of the government's policy to keep a tight grip of Chile's economic growth this year.
As the country's largest company, investments by Codelco have a huge impact on the economy and the foreign exchange market.
Projects in this year's investment plan include the expansion at the Andina mine and the clean-up plans at the Chuquicamata and El Teniente pits.
